sec-concepts.title: Map controls to CIA and control type
sec-concepts.code:
Control                         CIA goal         Type
------------------------------  ---------------  ----------
BitLocker on laptops            Confidentiality  Preventive
SHA-256 file integrity check    Integrity        Detective
Nightly backup + restore test   Availability     Corrective
CCTV at the server room door    Confidentiality  Detective
Signed purchase approvals       Non-repudiation  Preventive
sec-concepts.explanation: Classify every control by the goal it protects and how it acts. Gaps show up fast: here nothing deters, so a warning banner or visible guard would add a deterrent layer.

sec-threats.title: Dissect a spear-phishing email
sec-threats.code:
From: "Anna Cole (CFO)" <anna.cole@examp1e-corp.com>
Reply-To: anna.cole.cfo@gmail.com
Subject: URGENT - wire before 3pm

Please pay the attached invoice today. I'm in a board
meeting, so email only - don't call.
sec-threats.explanation: Four tells: a lookalike domain (examp1e), a Reply-To that differs from From, manufactured urgency, and a request to avoid the phone. The defence is a process rule: verify payment changes by calling a known number.

sec-malware.title: Read indicators from an EDR alert
sec-malware.code:
parent: WINWORD.EXE
child:  powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4A...
net:    TLS to 185.220.101.4:443 every 60s (+/-2s)
file:   C:\Users\ana\AppData\Roaming\upd.dll  (unsigned)
sec-malware.explanation: Office spawning encoded PowerShell, a periodic outbound connection (beaconing) and an unsigned DLL in a user-writable path together point to a macro dropper with C2. Isolate the host before cleaning it.

sec-iam.title: OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE
sec-iam.code:
1. App creates code_verifier (random) and code_challenge = SHA256(verifier)
2. Browser -> IdP /authorize?response_type=code&code_challenge=...
3. User signs in (MFA) -> IdP redirects back with ?code=abc123
4. App -> IdP /token  { code=abc123, code_verifier=... }
5. IdP checks SHA256(verifier) == challenge -> returns access + ID token
sec-iam.explanation: PKCE proves that whoever redeems the code is the same client that started the flow, so an intercepted code is useless. RFC 9700 recommends this flow for every client.

sec-architecture.title: Tokenise a card number
sec-architecture.code:
Checkout receives PAN   4111 1111 1111 1111
Vault stores           tok_8f3a29 -> 4111 1111 1111 1111
Order database keeps   tok_8f3a29   (shown as **** **** **** 1111)
Refunds call vault     tok_8f3a29 -> PAN, inside PCI scope only
sec-architecture.explanation: Only the vault ever sees the real card number, so the order database and analytics fall out of PCI scope. Masking (****1111) is for display; tokenisation removes the data.

sec-ops.title: Prioritise three findings
sec-ops.code:
Finding                       CVSS  KEV  Exposure          Priority
----------------------------  ----  ---  ----------------  --------
VPN RCE (CVE-2024-xxxx)       9.8   Yes  Internet-facing   1 (today)
HR app SQLi                   8.6   No   Internal only     2 (this sprint)
Dev laptop browser bug        6.5   No   Users only        3 (patch cycle)
sec-ops.explanation: CVSS alone would tie the first two. Known exploitation (KEV) and internet exposure make the VPN today's emergency.

cysa-soc-foundations.title: Triage an alert in five questions
cysa-soc-foundations.code:
Alert: 25 failed logons for svc_backup from 10.4.2.88, then 1 success
1. Is it real?        Source is a workstation; svc_backup only logs on from BKP01
2. What is affected?  Domain account with backup rights (high value)
3. Is it spreading?   Same source touched 3 servers in 10 min
4. Severity/priority? Credential compromise on a privileged account -> P1
5. Escalate?          Yes: Tier 2 + disable account per runbook
cysa-soc-foundations.explanation: A consistent triage script turns a noisy queue into decisions; asset value and spread set priority, not the alert's default severity.

cysa-vuln-basics.title: Compare credentialed and non-credentialed scans
cysa-vuln-basics.code:
Host 10.0.5.20 (Ubuntu 22.04)
Non-credentialed:  22/tcp OpenSSH 8.9p1 (banner)  -> 3 'possible' CVEs
Credentialed:      openssh-server 1:8.9p1-3ubuntu0.10 (dpkg)
                   -> 0 CVEs; vendor backported the fixes
cysa-vuln-basics.explanation: Banner checks guess from version strings and miss distribution backports; the authenticated scan reads the package database and removes the false positives.

cysa-siem-soar.title: A correlation rule (Sigma)
cysa-siem-soar.explanation: Neither event alone is interesting; the sequence from one IP within ten minutes is. Writing rules in Sigma lets you convert the same logic to Splunk, Sentinel or Elastic.

cysa-threat-hunting.title: Stack-count to find rare autoruns
cysa-threat-hunting.code:
SELECT run_key_value, COUNT(DISTINCT host) AS hosts
FROM autoruns
GROUP BY run_key_value
ORDER BY hosts ASC
LIMIT 10;

-- result: C:\Users\Public\svchost.exe   hosts = 1
cysa-threat-hunting.explanation: Legitimate software runs on hundreds of machines; an autorun seen on one host, in a public folder, with a system-binary name, is where to look first.

cysa-vuln-management.title: Risk-based ranking with EPSS and KEV
cysa-vuln-management.code:
CVE              CVSS  EPSS   KEV  Asset           Order
---------------  ----  -----  ---  --------------  -----
CVE-2023-4966    9.4   0.97   Yes  NetScaler edge  1
CVE-2024-1111    9.8   0.01   No   Isolated lab    3
CVE-2023-2222    7.5   0.62   No   Payment API     2
cysa-vuln-management.explanation: The 9.8 drops to last: almost no exploitation likelihood on an unreachable host. Likelihood (EPSS, KEV) times asset value drives the order.

cysa-incident-response.title: Contain a compromised host without losing evidence
cysa-incident-response.code:
1. EDR: network-isolate host FIN-WS-14 (keeps EDR channel)
2. Capture memory: winpmem.exe C:\ir\FIN-WS-14.raw
3. Hash it:         certutil -hashfile C:\ir\FIN-WS-14.raw SHA256
4. Log custody:     who, when, hash, storage location
5. Then image disk, then eradicate
cysa-incident-response.explanation: Isolation stops the spread while keeping the machine powered, so volatile memory (processes, keys, injected code) survives for analysis.

cysa-attack-frameworks.title: Map an incident to ATT&CK
cysa-attack-frameworks.code:
Observed                                   Tactic              Technique
-----------------------------------------  ------------------  ----------------
VPN login with stolen password             Initial Access      T1078 Valid Accounts
PowerShell download cradle                 Execution           T1059.001
Run key added                              Persistence         T1547.001
LSASS memory read                          Credential Access   T1003.001
Archive files to C:\temp\out.7z            Collection          T1074 Data Staged
cysa-attack-frameworks.explanation: Mapping turns a narrative into gaps: if you had no alert for T1003.001, that is your next detection to build.

cysa-reporting.title: An executive incident summary
cysa-reporting.code:
What happened:  Phishing led to one compromised finance mailbox (12 May).
Impact:         No payments made; 340 customer emails exposed.
Actions:        Account disabled in 20 min; mailbox rules removed; MFA enforced.
Obligations:    Legal assessing GDPR notification (72-hour clock started 12 May 10:00).
Next steps:     Phishing-resistant MFA for finance by 30 June (owner: IT Ops).
cysa-reporting.explanation: Five lines in business terms, with owners and dates. Hashes, IPs and log excerpts belong in the technical report, not here.

cissp-mindset.title: Choose the CISSP answer
cissp-mindset.code:
Scenario: A fire alarm sounds while you are mid-way through
imaging a compromised server for evidence.

A. Finish the image, then leave     (protects evidence)
B. Power the server off and leave   (protects data)
C. Leave immediately                (protects people)   <- answer
D. Call the CISO for a decision     (defers)
cissp-mindset.explanation: Life safety outranks evidence, data and systems every time. When several options are technically sensible, pick the one a manager responsible for people and the business would choose.

cissp-d1.title: Quantitative risk: is the control worth it?
cissp-d1.code:
Asset value (AV)            $500,000
Exposure factor (EF)        40%
SLE = AV x EF               $200,000
ARO (once every 4 years)    0.25
ALE = SLE x ARO             $50,000 per year

Control cost                $30,000 per year
ALE after control           $10,000 per year
Value = 50,000 - 10,000 - 30,000 = $10,000 per year  -> justified
cissp-d1.explanation: A control is worth buying when the reduction in ALE exceeds its annual cost. Present it to management in exactly these terms.

cissp-d1b.title: From BIA to recovery targets
cissp-d1b.code:
Function         MTD     RTO     RPO     Strategy
---------------  ------  ------  ------  -------------------------
Order taking     8 h     4 h     15 min  Warm site + log shipping
Payroll          5 days  2 days  24 h    Restore from nightly backup
Intranet wiki    14 days 7 days  1 week  Rebuild from weekly backup
cissp-d1b.explanation: The BIA sets MTD; RTO must fit inside it and RPO sets backup frequency. The strategy (and its cost) follows from those numbers, not the other way round.

cissp-d2.title: A data classification and handling table
cissp-d2.code:
Class         Example               Storage           Transmission     Disposal
------------  --------------------  ----------------  ---------------  -----------------
Restricted    Card data, health     Encrypted, MFA    TLS + DLP block  Purge or destroy
Confidential  Contracts, salaries   Encrypted         TLS              Purge
Internal      Policies, org chart   Access-controlled Any internal     Clear
Public        Marketing site        Any               Any              None
cissp-d2.explanation: The data owner assigns the class; the custodian applies the handling rules. Classification without handling rules changes nothing.

cissp-d2b.title: Sanitising media under NIST SP 800-88
cissp-d2b.code:
Media                      Leaving org?  Method
-------------------------  ------------  --------------------------------
HDD, reused internally     No            Clear  (single overwrite)
HDD, sold to recycler      Yes           Purge  (ATA Secure Erase) or destroy
SSD, any reuse             Either        Purge  (crypto erase / sanitize cmd)
SSD, end of life           Yes           Destroy (shred), with certificate
cissp-d2b.explanation: The method depends on where the media is going and the data's classification. Degaussing does nothing to SSDs.

cissp-d3.title: Bell-LaPadula vs Biba
cissp-d3.code:
Subject clearance: SECRET

Bell-LaPadula (confidentiality)
  read  TOP SECRET   -> denied   (no read up)
  write CONFIDENTIAL -> denied   (no write down)

Biba (integrity), subject integrity: MEDIUM
  read  LOW          -> denied   (no read down)
  write HIGH         -> denied   (no write up)
cissp-d3.explanation: The two models are mirror images: BLP stops secrets leaking down; Biba stops untrusted data contaminating trusted data.

cissp-d4.title: IPsec tunnel mode packet
cissp-d4.code:
Original:  [IP hdr 10.1.1.5 -> 10.2.2.9][TCP][data]

ESP tunnel mode:
[New IP 203.0.113.1 -> 198.51.100.7][ESP hdr][ IP 10.1.1.5 -> 10.2.2.9 | TCP | data ][ESP trailer][ICV]
                                             \_____________ encrypted _____________/
cissp-d4.explanation: Tunnel mode wraps and encrypts the whole original packet, hiding internal addresses between gateways; transport mode encrypts only the payload.

cissp-d5.title: Biometric error rates
cissp-d5.code:
Threshold   FRR (Type I)   FAR (Type II)
---------   ------------   -------------
Low         1%             8%
Medium      3%             3%   <- crossover error rate (CER)
High        9%             0.5%
cissp-d5.explanation: Raising sensitivity trades false acceptances for false rejections. The CER compares systems; a lower CER means a more accurate device. For a data-centre door, tune toward low FAR.

cissp-d6.title: Read a SOC 2 Type II report
cissp-d6.code:
Scope:     Production SaaS platform (not the mobile app)
Period:    1 Jan - 30 Jun
Criteria:  Security, Availability
Opinion:   Qualified
Exception: CC6.2 - 4 of 25 sampled leavers kept access > 5 days
CUECs:     Customer must manage its own user provisioning
cissp-d6.explanation: A 'SOC 2' claim tells you little. The scope, period, exceptions and complementary user entity controls (CUECs) tell you what was tested and what remains your job.

cissp-d7.title: Chain-of-custody record
cissp-d7.code:
Item:      Laptop SN 5CG1234XYZ, image file CASE-17-01.E01
SHA-256:   9f2c...e41a (acquisition) = 9f2c...e41a (verification)
2024-05-12 09:14  Collected by  J. Ortiz   from desk 4.12
2024-05-12 09:40  Imaged by     J. Ortiz   write-blocker WB-2
2024-05-12 10:05  Transferred   J. Ortiz -> evidence locker 3 (K. Lee)
Sealed bag no.  0047812
cissp-d7.explanation: Every handover is recorded with who, when and why, and the hash proves the image never changed. A gap in this record can make the evidence inadmissible.

cissp-cap-d1.title: A formal risk acceptance
cissp-cap-d1.code:
Risk:        Unpatched DB server ORDDB01 (CVE-2024-xxxx), no vendor patch
Compensating: Isolated VLAN, IPS signature, access from app tier only
Residual:    Medium
Owner:       VP Operations (signed)
Expiry:      90 days or vendor patch, whichever first
Review:      Monthly by security risk committee
cissp-cap-d1.explanation: Acceptance is a documented business decision with an owner, compensating controls and an expiry, never a silent 'we'll live with it'.

cissp-cap-d2.title: Safe test data
cissp-cap-d2.code:
-- copy production structure, not production people
INSERT INTO test.customers (id, name, email, card_last4)
SELECT id,
       'Customer ' || id,
       'user' || id || '@example.test',
       '0000'
FROM prod.customers TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1);
cissp-cap-d2.explanation: Test environments get masked or synthetic values that keep the shape of real data. Real PII in test is a breach waiting for an auditor.

cissp-cap-d3.title: Fail closed in code
cissp-cap-d3.explanation: When a security dependency breaks, the safe default is to deny. Returning True in the except branch would turn every outage into an open door.

cissp-cap-d4.title: Segment guest Wi-Fi
cissp-cap-d4.code:
VLAN 10  Corporate   10.10.0.0/16   802.1X (EAP-TLS)
VLAN 50  Guest       172.20.0.0/22  WPA3-Personal + captive portal

Firewall policy (zone guest):
  allow  guest -> internet : 80, 443
  deny   guest -> corporate: any   (log)
  deny   guest -> mgmt     : any   (log)
cissp-cap-d4.explanation: Guests are untrusted by definition, so the guest zone reaches the internet and nothing else; logging the denies shows anyone probing inward.

cissp-cap-d5.title: Step-up authentication policy
cissp-cap-d5.code:
Session: signed in with password + push MFA at 09:00

Action                       Requirement
---------------------------  ------------------------------
Read dashboards              existing session
Change payee bank details    re-authenticate with FIDO2 key
Add an admin role            FIDO2 + approval by second admin
Idle > 15 min                sign in again
cissp-cap-d5.explanation: MFA at login proves identity once; step-up and short idle timeouts bound what a stolen session can do, scaled to the risk of each action.

cissp-cap-d6.title: Choose the right test
cissp-cap-d6.code:
Question                                         Best test
-----------------------------------------------  ----------------------------
Are there flaws in our source before release?    SAST in CI
Is the running app exploitable by an attacker?   Authorised penetration test
Do our detections catch real techniques?         Breach & attack simulation
Did last month's patch still work?               Regression + rescan
cissp-cap-d6.explanation: Each test answers a different question. Pick it by what you need to prove, then make sure every finding gets an owner and a date.

cissp-cap-d7.title: First hour of a ransomware incident
cissp-cap-d7.code:
00:00  Declare incident; open bridge; assign IC and scribe
00:05  Isolate affected subnets (EDR network containment)
00:15  Preserve: memory from 2 hosts, firewall + EDR logs
00:20  Notify legal and leadership via out-of-band channel
00:30  Scope: which accounts, which data, is exfiltration seen?
00:45  Confirm backups are intact and offline
cissp-cap-d7.explanation: Contain first, preserve evidence, communicate out of band, then scope. Restoring before scoping usually brings the attacker back with the data.

cissp-cap-d8.title: Respond to a committed secret
cissp-cap-d8.code:
$ git log -p | grep -n 'AKIA'
  commit 3f9a... +AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...
1. Revoke the key in IAM now (assume it is compromised)
2. Review CloudTrail for its use since the commit time
3. Move secrets to a vault; inject at runtime
4. Add gitleaks as a pre-commit hook and in CI
cissp-cap-d8.explanation: Deleting the line does not help: the key is in history and any clone. Revoke first, investigate second, then fix the process so it cannot recur.
